# Ai Local Tools

Use only the rules that apply to the current consumer task.

## Contents

- [Generate local AI tools behind an authorization gate](#generate-local-ai-tools-behind-an-authorization-gate)

## Generate local AI tools behind an authorization gate

Declare stable application-owned tool contracts and let NewHeap generate local Microsoft.Extensions.AI functions that execute only after consumer authorization produces an explicit invocation scope.

## Preferred approach

Keep the tool method in consumer application code and delegate its query or
mutation to the normal application service. Add `NhAiToolSet` to the tool class,
and add `NhAiTool`, `Description`, an explicit version, effect, and exposure to
each method. Use lowercase dash-case for set and method IDs; the stable logical
ID is `<set>.<method>`.

Reference `NewHeap.Platform.AI.Generators` as an analyzer. The supported method
shape is `(input, NhAiInvocationContext, CancellationToken)` returning
`Task<TaskResult<T>>`. The generated catalog adapts that method to a local
`Microsoft.Extensions.AI.AIFunction`, emits canonical input/output schema and a
SHA-256 contract hash, and preserves the `TaskResult` outcome. Treat changes to
required fields, types, meaning, authorization, or effect as a new contract
version; use the generated catalog manifest as compatibility evidence.

For a trimmed Native AOT application, declare an application-owned
`JsonSerializerContext` that source-generates metadata for every tool input and
its `TaskResult<TOutput>`. Set that context through
`NhAiToolSet.JsonSerializerContextType`. This keeps function argument and result
serialization reflection-free after trimming; omitting required metadata can
make function creation or invocation fail only in the published executable.

Register an `INhAiToolInvocationGate` and `INhAiToolInvoker` before creating
functions. The gate must validate the current actor and derive tenant, division,
or resource scope server-side. The tool receives that authorized scope through
`NhAiInvocationContext`; request input is never authorization evidence. Keep the
first exposure local unless a separately reviewed transport and discovery policy
exists. Telemetry records tool ID, version, effect, exposure, and outcome only.

Set a bounded `MaxInputBytes` for each contract and keep the generated typed
argument binding as the runtime schema boundary. The shared invoker serializes
the bound arguments with the platform JSON policy and rejects oversized input
before capability, approval, budget, idempotency, or application work. Every
invocation also reserves through `INhAiBudgetManager`; omitting an optional
remaining-run budget never disables that reservation. Startup fails when a
profile or catalog is registered without a real budget manager.

Register an explicit `INhAiToolDiscoveryPolicy` for every model-visible catalog.
The platform default denies all discovery. Filter for one exposure boundary at a
time, derive scope and capability grants outside model input, and repeat
authorization during invocation to prevent time-of-check/time-of-use bypasses.

For mutation tools, declare approval, idempotency, verifier, timeout,
concurrency, input-size, result-size, classification, retention, and capability
metadata on the attribute. Every non-read effect requires idempotency. Generic
mutation, external-side-effect, and destructive effects also require approval;
destructive effects require a verifier. Generated catalogs attest
`SharedInvoker` governance and return descriptor-bound governed functions.
MCP and Agent adapters reject raw, mismatched, or ungoverned functions.

## Avoid

- Calling controllers or bypassing the normal application service from a tool.
- Accepting a tenant or division from model input as proof of authorization.
- Registering an allow-all production gate or creating functions without a gate.
- Omitting the budget manager or assuming a missing remaining-run budget means unlimited execution.
- Hand-writing an attested catalog around a function that does not actually call `INhAiToolInvoker`.
- Exposing a tool through MCP or an agent merely because a local catalog exists.
- Logging prompts, arguments, model output, secrets, or full exception content.
- Returning ad-hoc exceptions for expected business outcomes instead of `TaskResult`.

## Verification

Build the consumer project so the generator and its `NHAI` diagnostics run.
Assert the generated descriptor ID, version, effect, exposure, authorization,
schema, and manifest metadata. Exercise both an authorized invocation and a denied or incomplete
scope, and verify the latter never reaches the application service. Also verify
an unauthorized tool is absent from discovery. For mutations, also exercise
proposal binding, duplicate retries, and verifier disagreement. Exercise an
oversized input, a denied budget reservation, and an ungoverned catalog; none may
reach the application service. SPM-234
publishes the generated catalog through a trimmed Native AOT smoke executable
and invokes a generated function so reflection-free descriptors, schemas,
manifests, argument binding, and result serialization remain rooted.
SPM-219, SPM-221, SPM-224, SPM-234, and the `NewHeap.Platform.AI.Tests`
project are the executable references.
